analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (26.10.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 52bps to 7623 (+11.4% YTD) on an ongoing tech selloff. GS US colleagues saw an aggregate $20bn net TMT selling over 2 weeks across all client types.
Cross-asset: US 10yr yield lower at 4.97%, Brent $115 on escalation fears, Gold $4013, Bitcoin $80k (also risk-off).
Busy week ahead: Fed rate decision Wednesday, 20% of the S&P and important non-US stocks report. SkHynix, Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday. Samsung, Amazon and Intel report Thursday.

Middle East: Iran escalation risk is higher. Brent rose on reports that the US and Israel are moving toward a renewed joint campaign that could begin in coming days and include Iranian ports alongside nuclear, missile and energy targets. The US also warned Iraq's Prime Minister of possible airstrikes against Iran.

AI tokenomics: Ramp reports 2 consecutive months of virtually no growth in token spending while token volumes kept rising. Falling effective prices and a shift to more efficient models appear to absorb much of the usage growth.

Gavin Baker argued on X that falling token prices alone do not imply weaker GPU demand. The relevant measure is revenue per GPU (token price times token throughput) relative to GPU rental cost. Faster inference and a shift to lower-margin open-weight models can raise compute needed per dollar of end-customer revenue.

Fed (Wed meeting): GS expects the FOMC to skip raising rates and likely deliver a second hike in December. The key question is how the statement changes the sentence referring to the September hike. No significant new information is expected from the press conference.
Nvidia: good Jensen keynote at GTC Berlin. A robotics demo used Hermes Agent on RTX Spark to orchestrate simulation, cloud training and deployment for Hugging Face's Microduck robots.
a16z article on GPUs: GPU prices are 9% to 143% higher than they would have been had the chips depreciated steadily over the supposed 6-year life.

Credit podcast with GS chief credit strategist Amanda Lynam: spreads could be 'a bit wider from now until early December and then things should tighten a bit when the new issuance machine shuts down'. Discussion covered cost and availability of capital to fund AI capex.

Kospi: GS lowers its target from 12k to 9k on more conservative assumptions about how the market prices fundamentals. The 9k target implies 6.5x consensus forward P/E and 1.5x P/B vs 23% ROE. GS still sees attractive risk/reward and views Korean equities as deeply undervalued.

Amazon: CEO Jassy says AWS 2026 cloud capacity is sold out, most large 2027 capacity blocks are booked, and a meaningful share of 2028 is committed. This supports demand for chips, memory and networking.
US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (4 of the last 5), mainly through long and short sales in single stocks, which saw the largest de-grossing since late July.

Retail trading volumes in US equities are down 20% since the summer and 45% since late 2025, attributed to weak consumer sentiment and elevated energy prices. Equity options and prediction markets are growing alternatives, with monthly prediction market volume at $78bn in Sep26 vs $5bn in Sep25.
Momentum factor stat: the GS momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) has had 30 daily moves of +/-5% in 2026, more than any other year in the dataset (including 2000, 2009 and 2020), with 2 months left.
US long/short net leverage fell 0.3pts to 43.4%, the 0th percentile over 5 years.
Musk on X: 'I think we're going to see a lot of stranded compute in partially complete data centers'.
